policy_rows.selected: {"consequence":"A concrete draft gives singers something specific to assess while leaving time to correct avoidable attendance problems.","decision":"How should rehearsal dates be chosen from available room slots?","mechanism":"The booking organizer proposes a sequence of available room slots, and members identify conflicts before reservations are finalized."}

{"consequence":"Confirmation is prompted at a predictable time, making the expected numbers easier to use during final preparation.","decision":"How should expected attendance reach the conductor?","mechanism":"The organizer sends a rehearsal reminder with an attendance response link and summarizes replies for the conductor."}

{"consequence":"Singers can prepare early while anyone who needs paper still receives the same music before singing begins.","decision":"How should singers obtain the music needed for rehearsal?","mechanism":"The organizer sends the numbered score list and digital copies before rehearsal, with matching paper copies available at arrival."}

{"consequence":"Reports from different voice parts shape the order before the full choir spends time on the selected difficulties.","decision":"How should the order of rehearsal pieces be set?","mechanism":"The conductor asks section leaders which prepared pieces need attention and then publishes a balanced rehearsal sequence."}

{"consequence":"Responsibility is shared across the choir while the fixed sequence keeps the brief preparation coordinated and predictable.","decision":"Who should guide the shared vocal warmup?","mechanism":"Different section leaders each guide one part of the approved warmup in a posted order."}

{"consequence":"The final arrangement responds to the room’s sound while preserving each singer’s part and view of the conductor.","decision":"How should chairs be arranged within voice sections?","mechanism":"The conductor listens to a short phrase and then asks singers to adjust chairs within their sections."}

{"consequence":"The part needing direct attention receives it without leaving the remaining singers idle during that practice block.","decision":"How should short sectional practice be organized?","mechanism":"The conductor works with one section while the other section leaders guide their own assigned passages in separate corners."}

{"consequence":"A single diagnosis concentrates practice time on the feature the conductor judges most responsible for the difficulty.","decision":"How should a difficult passage be diagnosed?","mechanism":"The conductor listens to the passage and chooses one element for the choir to isolate before recombining it."}

{"consequence":"Singers begin with the shared rehearsal problem and select their own line from the materials associated with it.","decision":"How should practice recordings be made easy to use?","mechanism":"The conductor groups approved recordings by difficult passage and lists each available voice part within that passage."}

{"consequence":"A written reminder is established before the choir tries to follow the same gesture in real time.","decision":"How should singers learn shared entrances and cutoffs?","mechanism":"The conductor demonstrates each entrance and cutoff while singers mark the matching cue in their scores before singing."}

{"consequence":"Rotating invitations give each part a clear opportunity to describe the balance from its listening position.","decision":"How should singers offer observations about musical balance?","mechanism":"The conductor asks one section at a time what it heard after a combined passage and then decides adjustments."}

{"consequence":"Immediate personal notes are followed by a common confirmation that can correct misheard instructions before everyone leaves.","decision":"How should changes to score markings be kept consistent?","mechanism":"Singers mark changes during rehearsal, and the conductor reviews the affected bars aloud before the organizer publishes the change record."}

{"consequence":"The same concise package lets each person catch up independently at a time compatible with their other commitments.","decision":"How should an absent singer catch up?","mechanism":"Absent singers receive the rehearsal notes and use the linked change record and recordings before returning."}

{"consequence":"The pause follows a coherent piece of musical work while remaining predictable within the published rehearsal sequence.","decision":"How should the main rehearsal break be timed?","mechanism":"The conductor places the planned break after a named rehearsal block and announces that position at the start."}

{"consequence":"Responsibility moves among willing members, and each person knows in advance which part of the room to prepare.","decision":"How should room setup duties be shared?","mechanism":"The organizer assigns setup duties through a rotating volunteer list and sends reminders before each rehearsal."}

{"consequence":"Singers leave with a limited, specific task that can be found again without remembering an extended spoken explanation.","decision":"How should the choir agree what to practice before next time?","mechanism":"The conductor names two practice priorities at the end and includes the relevant bars in the rehearsal notes."}
